Together, we make a difference
Latest News
Welcome to our school!
We're so happy to have you with us! Whether you're just starting your journey with us or have been part of our school family for some time, we want you to know that you're always at the heart of everything we do. Our school is a place where curiosity, creativity, and kindness come together to create a safe and inspiring environment for everyone.
Here, we believe in nurturing not only academic growth but personal growth, too. We encourage each of our students to explore their passions, ask questions, and discover new things. Alongside our dedicated staff, we work hard to build a supportive, inclusive community where everyone is valued and every voice matters. Thank you for being part of our school. Together, we're making this a place where learning and friendship flourish.

pageCache.pageTitle: New Milton Infant School - Wraparound Childcare - Breakfast & After School Clubs
pageCache.text:
Breakfast and After School Clubs
Breakfast Club
New Milton Infant School pupils can attend the Breakfast Club which is run by New Milton Junior School and is open from 7:45am until the start of school, at which time the Infant School children will be accompanied by staff across the school field to the Infant School.
Sessions are £4 per day, and include a breakfast of cereal or toast, plus apple and orange juice. To book a place, please go to the New Milton Junior School website via the link below for more information on how to book Breakfast club sessions.
New Milton Junior School Breakfast Club
There is a booking form on the Junior School webpage. Please contact the Junior School office on newmiltonjuniorschool.co.uk or tel 01425 614633 when you wish to book for the first time as they will need to set you up on their SCOPAY payment system.
Twilight Club - After School Club
Twilight Club is an OFSTED registered Wraparound Childcare after school club for children who attend both New Milton Infant School and New Milton Junior schools. Twilight Club is managed and led by qualified staff from our school offering a fun, warm and homely environment underpinned by our Aspirations.
Twilight Club is open from 3:15-6pm on school days and is located at New Milton Infant School. We accept Tax-Free Childcare Credits and Childcare vouchers towards the cost of club sessions.
OFSTED Registration Number 115928
New Milton Junior School Pupils
If your child currently attends New Milton Junior school, and you would like to register them for the first time this academic year to Twilight club, please complete our registration form below to provide information about you and your child so that we can set you up on our Arbor online booking system.
ENROLMENTS FOR 26/27 TWILIGHT CLUB NOW OPEN
If you would like to be able to book sessions at our Twilight club during the 26/27 academic year, and your child will be a NM Junior School pupil, you will need to complete our 26/27 Twilight Club enrolment form so that club sessions will be open for you to book onto. Please complete our online form via the link below to register your Junior child.
As we are now on our Summer break, 26/27 registration forms will be processed when school staff return to school on 1st September, and you will still have time to book before the first Twilight Club session on 3rd September.26/27 Twilight Club Membership Form For New Milton Junior School Pupils
Children who are pupils at New Milton Infant School can be booked onto Twilight Club straight away.
There are two available options for sessions:-
We will offer your child a light snack, however this does not replace a main meal.
All sessions must be booked and paid for in advance using the Infant School Arbor Portal (not NM Junior Arbor) . You will need to top-up your Arbor childcare account balance using your bank card before you can book sessions, unless you have previously advised us that you are eligible for Tax-Free Childcare credits.
Parents of Junior school children will need to complete our Twilight Club Registration Form (see link above) so that we can register you on the Infant School Arbor portal.
We are able to accept Tax-Free Childcare Credits and Childcare vouchers, however you must notify the infant school office prior to booking your first session if you intend to use these methods of payment so that we can open this facility on your Arbor account.
Please read the document below before booking onto the club to ensure you can comply and are happy with our club terms and conditions.
Twilight Club Terms & Conditions for Parents 2026-2027
How to Sign up to Wraparound Clubs on Your Arbor Portal

Emergency Telephone Number
If your child is in Twilight Club and you have an emergency, (For example if you will be delayed due to an unexpected emergency event), you can contact the Twilight Club staff out of school hours on our emergency telephone number which is 07598457093
Please do not use this number for general booking or payment queries as these queries can be dealt with by the school office team.
Tax Free Childcare
Many working parents are entitled to help towards childcare costs under the government's "Tax-Free Childcare" scheme. Eligible working parents who can get a £2 top-up for every £8 towards the cost of their childcare.
Further information and guidance on Tax Free Childcare including an eligibility checker can be found on the HM Government webpage:
https://www.beststartinlife.gov.uk/childcare-early-years-education/tax-free-childcare
Our registration for Tax Free Childcare comes under Hampshire County Council whose Unique Tax Reference (UTR) is 3111347356
The address which should be used is: The Castle, Winchester, SO23 8UJ. Bank details are 62-28-49 (sort code) and 00000000 (account number).
If you are eligible for Tax-Free childcare, please email your Tax-Free Childcare reference number (eg ABC1234568D to the school office so we can set the facility up for you to pay for your sessions using Tax-Free Childcare credits. You can then arrange to transfer funds from your Government childcare account into your Arbor portal childcare account to pay for the cost of your booked sessions.

pageCache.text:
Pupil Premium (aka Free School Meals)
Your child may be eligible for Pupil Premium (Income based free school meals) if you get any of the following state benefits:
* UPDATED FREE SCHOOL MEAL ELIGIBILITY
From September 2026, the eligibility criteria for free school meals (FSM) will expand to include pupils living in households in receipt of Universal Credit with an income above the current £7,400 threshold.
We recommend all parents check their entitlement to Pupil Premium as all eligible children will receive additional support in school to improve children's educational outcomes, as well as many other perks including a free school bookbag and free holiday activity clubs. In addition the school receives additional funding to provide additional support to qualifying pupils.
Why do I need to register, don't all infant children get free school meals?
Many families miss out on the advantages of registering for Pupil Premium (Income Based Free School Meals) due to the confusion with the Universal Infant Free School Meals that gives all Infant aged children a free school lunch regardless of their family income.
The Income-based Free School Meals is a separate scheme which applies to children from lower-incomes families only to help increase the educational outcomes of children from a disadvantaged background. By registering your child when they are at Infant School, this will ensure a smooth transition when they move to Junior school, where school meals are normally chargeable.
Link to Hampshire County Council's Free School Meal Web Page
Free School Meal Eligibility Checker
To check your child's eligibility for pupil premium or continued free school meals (from Key Stage 2), use the online eligibility checker above.
To complete an eligibility check you need the following information for yourself or the person you are checking on behalf of:
If you would prefer the school to perform this check for you, please provide the school office with your personal information above and we will be happy to check on your behalf.
How can I check if I am Eligible for Income Based Free School Meals?
To see if you are eligible for Income based Free School Meals (Pupil Premium) please click on the link above. It is best to check your eligibility than miss out!
Are there any other benefits to Registering my Child for Free School Meals (Pupil Premium)?
Yes, in addition to receiving additional educational support, all children registered for Pupil Premium (Income-based free school meals) are also eligible to attend local holiday activities clubs free of charge during school holidays via the Hampshire County Council Holidays and Activities and Food Fund. (HAF) Please see the HAF webpage to find out more.https://www.hants.gov.uk/socialcareandhealth/childrenandfamilies/connectforcommunities/holidayactivities

pageCache.pageTitle: New Milton Infant School - Personal, Social & Health Education
pageCache.text:
Personal, Social & Health Education
"Promise me you'll always remember: you're braver than you believe, and stronger than you seem, and smarter than you think" - Christopher Robin.
Intent
To support the children in Personal, Social, Health Education (PSHE) and Relationships and Sex Education (RSE) we have chosen to follow the NHS-backed My Happy Mind mindfulness scheme, in which many teachers using the scheme nationally have seen an improvement in children’s resilience and perseverance. This is a comprehensive whole school approach for PSHE including statutory Relationships and Health Education. It is a fully planned progressive scheme of work, focused on building resilience, self-esteem, and happiness in children. We have chosen this approach because it uses preventative strategies firmly rooted in science, research, and the fields of neuroscience and positive psychology. In addition to My Happy Mind, we teach the children about the Zones of Regulation throughout their school journey, how to identify what their body or mind might be feeling when they are in each of the zones (green, blue, yellow, red and orange), and which tools they might utilise to help them.
Implementation
Mental health activity is often focused on supporting individuals when they face challenges. Whilst this is critical, we believe that it is also important to support individuals in building their resilience and self-esteem proactively. My Happy Mind is split into five themes:
Children will be able to readily choose how to respond to situations rather than just react, helping them make good behaviour choices, concentrate on their work and lessen stress and anxiety. My Happy Mind complements our school Aspirations ‘I am courageous’, ‘I am responsible’, ‘I am respectful’, ‘I try my best’, and ‘I am kind’, that are taught and woven into our school lives.
We believe that effective RSE is essential to enable our children to make responsible and well-informed decisions about their lives. These lessons are not delivered in isolation but are firmly rooted in our PSHE curriculum through My Happy Mind. The aim of RSE is to help and support children through their physical, emotional and moral development.
The children are supported to develop the vocabulary and confidence needed to clearly articulate their thoughts and feelings in a climate of openness, trust and respect, and know when and how they can seek support from others. They develop and apply their understanding to their interactions with each other, small groups, the whole class and to the wider community of which they are a part.
My Happy Mind is a whole school approach, with all year groups working on the same theme at the same time. These themes each cover a half-term of work. Each key stage teaches lessons in an age appropriate way so that they meet the children's needs.
There is a clear progression of social, moral and cultural understanding across the school. Each lesson is taught as a whole class. An important feature of My Happy Mind is to ensure that all children are taught as a class in a calm, safe environment and each session follows the same structure. During My Happy Mind sessions, all children are encouraged to speak freely in front of the class group, encouraging clear communication. Respect and tolerance of others is expected and children are given time to reflect on their learning and themselves as people.
Other school initiatives that support the development of PSHE include:

NSPCC; Speak Out Stay Safe
Children's Mental Health Week
Internet safety
Clever Never Goes - stranger danger
Aspirations assemblies

Helping hands
Using mindfulness journals
Utilising breathing exercises
Impact
The impact of our PSHE teaching is evident in school life as a whole - in the children's behaviour, their attitudes to learning and their respect and care and understanding for and of each other. It is evaluated through monitoring change and development of behaviour, assessing strands of PSED in the Early Years Foundation Stage and assessing the themes of the My Happy Mind curriculum in Key Stage 1.

pageCache.pageTitle: New Milton Infant School - Family Support Worker
pageCache.text:
Family Support Worker
My name is Rachel Baker. I am the Family Support Worker for New Milton Infant School.
What does a Family Support Worker do?
I offer impartial support, advice and guidance to parents and carers. I am a School-based service that provides free support with:
• Parenting concerns
• Confidence building
• Relationship breakdown
• Accessing local services
• Behaviour management
• School holiday activities
• Benefits / housing / Debt.
I also support children on a 1:1 basis, listening and working with them in different ways e.g.
Anger management and control
Key transitions, including moving between schools/classes
Development of pupil self-esteem and confidence
Friendship issues / bullying, including social networking
Family issues: bereavement, new baby in the family, parent’s separation / divorce.
As a Family Support Worker I give support to families in many different ways including:
One-to-one working with parents and carers including talking, listening and supporting
Finding practical strategies with parents/carers and children to improve learning, behaviour and relationships
Referring and signposting to local services
Drop-in coffee mornings.
Why might you need to contact me?
As parents/carers, every day a new challenge or question may arise and you may wonder what the answer or solution is.
"My child's behaviour is getting out of control"
"I'm worried about parents evening"
"Since my partner left, things haven't been the same"
"I'm worried about my child"
"I would just like someone to share my concerns with"
If you would like a friendly chat, I can be found on the playground before school.
Alternatively, please contact me to make an appointment on 01425 610568 or leave a message for me at the school office.
Positive Parenting 'Time Out for Parents'
We are pleased to announce that our Family Support Worker (FSW), Mrs Baker has been successfully trained to deliver Positive Parenting Time Out for Parents courses from Care for the Family.
This amazing six week course provides jargon-free information and ideas to help you engage with your children and boost your relationship. If you have children aged 5 to 11, then ‘Time Out for Parents – The Primary Years’ is for you. Over six sessions, you will increase your skills and confidence as a parent and discover practical tools to make your relationship with your child even better.
The sessions are as follows;
Session 1 What being a parent’s really like
Session 2 Children’s needs
Session 3 Feelings and listening
Session 4 Boundaries and parenting styles
Session 5 Keeping children safe
Session 6 Building strong families
Rachel Baker (Family Support Worker) 01425 610568 r.baker@nmis.hants.sch.uk

pageCache.pageTitle: New Milton Infant School - Class Dojo
pageCache.text:
Class Dojo
Class Dojo is a school communication platform that teachers and families use every day to build close-knit communities by sharing what's being learned in the classroom through photos, videos and messages.
As well as having a main school page where notices, announcements and reminders are shared, each class has their own individual Dojo page. The online classrooms are created and parents are then invited to connect to the class through an individual, personalised link. Once connected, parents can see their child's class page where teachers will share updates and photos about what the children have been doing at school. It is important to note that these pages are not public, they are private and can only be viewed by connected staff and by parents of children in the same class.
Once connected, parents will be able to make use of the direct messaging section that allows them to directly contact their child's class teacher. This is a very useful tool that supports effective communication between home and school.
Dojo points
At school children have the opportunity to earn Dojo points when they show our values and behaviour rules. They receive a bronze certificate when they achieve 25 Dojo points, silver certificate when they achieve 50 Dojo points, a gold certificate when they achieve 75 Dojo points and a platinum certificate when they achieve 100 Dojo points. In addition, each class decides on a whole class reward when they collectively achieve an agreed amount.
